Possible-ancestor/descendant node-set queries

Source: R/queries.R
possible-queries.Rd

possible_ancestors() finds every node V for which some DAG (for a PDAG-family cg) or MAG (for a PAG cg) in the equivalence class represented by cg has V as an ancestor of node: nodes reachable from node by a possibly directed path, one on which no edge is compelled in the direction away from node (traversing an undirected edge, or a directed/circle edge oriented, or possibly orientable, toward node). possible_descendants() is the mirror notion in the other direction. Both are supersets of ancestors()/descendants(), since those only count edges compelled in the right direction.

Usage

possible_ancestors(cg, node, open = getOption("CausalStructures.open", TRUE))

possible_descendants(cg, node, open = getOption("CausalStructures.open", TRUE))

Arguments

cg

A PDAG-family (PDAG, CPDAG, MPDAG) or PAG graph created with cgraph().

node

Node name.

open

If TRUE (default, from the CausalStructures.open option), exclude node itself from the result; if FALSE, include it.

Value

Sorted character vector of node names.

References

Perković E, Textor J, Kalisch M, Maathuis MH (2018). “Complete Graphical Characterization and Construction of Adjustment Sets in Markov Equivalence Classes of Ancestral Graphs.” Journal of Machine Learning Research, 18, 1–62.

Examples

if (julia_ready()) {
  cpdag <- cgraph(A %---% B, B %---% C, class = "CPDAG")
  list(
    ancestors = ancestors(cpdag, "C"),
    possible_ancestors = possible_ancestors(cpdag, "C"),
    possible_ancestors_including_self =
      possible_ancestors(cpdag, "C", open = FALSE)
  )
}
#> $ancestors
#> character(0)
#> 
#> $possible_ancestors
#> [1] "A" "B"
#> 
#> $possible_ancestors_including_self
#> [1] "A" "B" "C"
#>
